title: The House of Heine Brothers, in Munich

cognitive_validation.rationale: The banking operations and partnership are rendered with coherent, systematic, nonsupernatural social and economic logic, but this coherence is simply that of ordinary realism rather than an imaginary novum.

novum_candidates.description: The banking house of Heine Brothers and the granting of a partnership to Herbert Onslow, which resolves the marriage plot.
novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: The narrator's contrasts between English and German banking and between English and German manners create reader-facing contrast, but these are comparative cultural observations within a realist frame, not cognitive estrangement produced by a novum.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The partnership question drives the central marriage plot: the delay frustrates Herbert, and the eventual grant of the partnership resolves the story. It is narratively central, but centrality alone does not make it a novum absent novelty.

novelty.rationale: A 19th-century Munich banking firm and the conferral of a business partnership are entirely consistent with the author's empirical realist norm. There is no totalizing or world-altering difference from the empirical world; this is a mundane commercial and domestic arrangement.
